coreConcepts.text: As of November 2026: OpenAI's GPT-6 line (Astra at the top, with 6.1 Sol and Terra below it and Luna as the fast tier), Anthropic's Claude line (Fable 5.2 at the top, then Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5), and Google's Gemini 4 line (Carbon, Argon, Hydrogen). Independent trackers score them within a few points of each other.
coreConcepts.title: Three Families At The Frontier

coreConcepts.text: A fast, cheap model for volume work; a frontier workhorse for everyday hard tasks; and a deep-thinking model that spends longer per answer for the hardest problems. Pick the tier by task, not by brand loyalty.
coreConcepts.title: Every Vendor Ships The Same Three Tiers

coreConcepts.text: Top models now take around a million tokens in one interaction — whole document sets, not single files. Long-context quality still varies, so verify on your own material, but 'it won't fit' is rarely the blocker now.
coreConcepts.title: Context Is No Longer The Constraint It Was

coreConcepts.text: Some of the most capable models are gated: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber and Anthropic's Mythos are limited to vetted security and life-sciences organizations. If a workflow depends on a model you cannot access, it is not part of your real options.
coreConcepts.title: Restricted Models Are A New Category

artifact.title: Open versus closed decision prompts

commonMistakes: Saying 'open source' when the accurate term is open-weight, with a license that has conditions.
Assuming open-weight means free; serving and maintaining a large model is real infrastructure work.
Choosing on capability alone when a data-boundary rule already decided the question.

coreConcepts.text: The model's weights are published for download under a license, so you (or a host) can run it on your own infrastructure. Open-weight is not the same as open source: training data and full training code are usually not included, and licenses vary.
coreConcepts.title: What Open-Weight Means

coreConcepts.text: The top closed models (GPT-6, Claude Fable, Gemini 4) still lead on independent capability indexes, and they come as a managed service: no infrastructure, fast updates, enterprise agreements, and support. You pay per use, and your data flows through the vendor under their terms.
coreConcepts.title: What Closed Buys You

coreConcepts.text: Open-weight wins on control: data stays in your boundary, costs are predictable at scale, and the model cannot be deprecated out from under you. Closed wins on capability, convenience, and safety infrastructure. Gated models (GPT-6 Cyber, Claude Mythos) are a third bucket: closed, and restricted to vetted users.
coreConcepts.title: The Real Tradeoffs

coreConcepts.text: Closed models get retired on vendor schedules — Google deprecated Gemini 2.5 in November 2026 and reroutes requests to newer versions. A workflow pinned to a closed model needs a migration plan; a workflow on open weights needs a maintenance plan instead.
coreConcepts.title: Deprecation Risk Cuts Both Ways

artifact.label: Protocol
artifact.title: Five-minute release check

commonMistakes: Switching tools on launch day based on a single benchmark.
Ignoring gated availability until after the workflow is redesigned around an inaccessible model.
Missing a deprecation notice until the old model stops answering.

coreConcepts.text: Every launch mixes a capability claim, an availability claim, and a price claim. Check each separately: a model can be real, excellent, and still not available to you (gated) or not worth its price tier.
coreConcepts.title: Separate The Three Claims

coreConcepts.text: Artificial Analysis and similar trackers give a common yardstick across vendors, and human-preference rankings add a second view. Treat any single number as a signal, not a verdict — small gaps rarely survive contact with your actual tasks.
coreConcepts.title: Use Independent Scorecards, Carefully

coreConcepts.text: Deprecations, price changes, and limit changes affect your workflows more than flagship launches do. The most useful release-note habit is scanning for what is being taken away.
coreConcepts.title: Watch The Quiet News

coreConcepts.text: Keep two or three representative tasks with known-good outputs. Run any candidate model on them before switching a workflow. Ten minutes of task-level evidence beats an afternoon of launch threads.
coreConcepts.title: Test On Your Own Work
